text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Mubarak at the Davos forum requests the creation of a new international atmosphere that would protect the economies of developing countries. The president gives a speech at Davos, says peace is like a holy obligation for Egypt. At the international press conference: I felt some pessimism on Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's part about Israeli practices after the Hebron deal.
- At a meeting of the political club of the ruling National Democratic Party: the court's verdict that privatisation is constitutional wipes out all the excuses of those opposed to it.
- International Monetary Fund official says Egypt's economic growth rate will reach five percent this year and the reducing the budget deficit came as a suprise to the fund.

- Mubarak tells the Davos forum: Egypt will not turn back from its mission to become part of the global economy. We are certain of the validity of our economic restructuring programme and we are committed to it. After 15 years of reforms, we are now moving towards making the lives of the people easier.
- Mubarak at the international press conference at Davos: Implementing the peace deals creates confidence and drives the negotiations on the Syrian track.
- Mubarak met with Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. The president: my talks with Netanyahu gave me hope for the peace process.
- International Monetary Fund: We will give Egypt any help or any loans it asks for. Egypt is the only country that did not face negative effects of economic reforms.

- Mubarak at the international Davos forum: Peace has to be just and provide help for all. We need a region that is free from fear, aggression and total destruction. Our policy is based on increasing investments and opening the economy further to the world. Our economic reform programme is ambitious and presents opportunities to the foreign investor. Debt service leaves poor countries with little funds to develop with.
- Mubarak after meeting Netanyahu: Syrian-Israeli peace talks can resume at any time.
- The head of the Davos forum lauds Mubarak's courage and wisdom.
- Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi says terrorist incidents fell in 1996 by 70 percent compared to the previous year.
